properties.name: MEASURED 2026-09-28 (static): four edge types are two to four different relations under one name, split by a property value on each edge — so the per-TYPE reading just declared is right for only part of their instances, and any rule moved onto readings would inherit the error
properties.source: three-graph primitives classification, 2026-09-28 (primitives repo github.com/sligara7/primitives, analysis/synthesis/reflow2-edge-readings-for-review.md and analysis/classified/reflow2/notes.md), items re-verified in schema and code
properties.statement:
Found while building req:every-edge-type-declares-what-it-means, from the three-graph classification's review sheet (its medium-confidence rows) and re-checked against schema and code at origin/main 329a074:
1. CAUSES carries `basis` ∈ {observed, correlational, causal, spurious}, DEFAULT correlational (schema/inference.yaml:28). An unannotated CAUSES edge therefore asserts a correlation, and `spurious` asserts that there is NO causal link — while the declared reading says causes(+). edge_types_read_as("causes", …) returns CAUSES regardless.
2. CONTRADICTS with `alignment: supporting` means corroboration — the opposite relation — and two code paths filter it back out by hand (heal.rs:1950, report.rs:2253). Precedent: dec:idea-how-should-one-finding-say-it-corroborates-another.
3. AUTHORED_BY `role=approver` is the owner's signature on an ACCEPTED node (read by the intent-authority gate), but on a PROPOSED Decision it means the person was ASKED to settle it (report.rs:431, the assigned-decisions count). Same edge, same role value, two relations, told apart by the target's status. Roles were already made a set once because one relation per edge was losing facts.
4. INTERACTS_WITH is an umbrella: each `interaction` value reads cleanly (three as flows-to, `triggers` as causes); unset, it asserts only that some relation exists (its reading is `leftover`).
CONSEQUENCE: a per-type reading cannot be right for these four. Before any existing rule moves onto readings (the follow-up PR), a reading needs a per-value split — the classification scheme already has the field for it (`subtypes`, one reading per value of the splitting property) — and selection must honour it per edge instance, not per type.

CORRECTION, same evening (2026-09-28): FOUR UNDERCOUNTS IT. "Four" came from the review sheet's medium-confidence rows. The classification's own records (analysis/classified/reflow2/records.jsonl, the `subtypes` field) give a value-dependent reading for more edges, each re-checked against the schema at 329a074:
- A DIFFERENT PRIMITIVE by value, six more:
  - DEPENDS_ON.dependency_type: function_call and control_flow read causes[initiating]; data_flow and error_flow read flows-to; physical reads causes[necessary].
  - CHANGED.action: added reads source-of(made); modified reads causes; removed reads causes(−).
  - YIELDED.action: created reads source-of; updated reads causes; merged reads same-as.
  - ANNOTATES.note_kind: author reads about; reviewer reads about ∧ stance; director reads about ∧ norm.binds.
  - DUPLICATES.basis: asserted licenses same-as; suspected, the default, is only a comparison.
  - VIOLATES_RULE.status: confirmed adds a permitting norm, a waiver, on top of norm.meets(−).
- A DIFFERENT MODALITY by value, five: SATISFIES.coverage=planned, DEPLOYED_TO.status, REQUIRES_RESOURCE.criticality, GOVERNED_BY.ruling=parks, SCHEDULED_FOR.modality.
- Split by something ON THE FAR END, which a split on the edge's own properties cannot see, three: AUTHORED_BY approver (the target's status), CONTAINS (the source's type: project scope vs component structure), SCHEDULED_FOR (a Release target).

The CAUSES `basis=observed` reading also conflicts. The classifier read it as causes, observed but not explained. The split first written into the schema reads it as co-occurrence. Nothing in the schema, the code or docs/chain-reflow-nuggets.md defines `observed`, and no code reads any basis value.
